items.stem: When is recording a macro the better starting point rather than writing VBA from scratch?

options.text: For a simple, repetitive UI task where you can learn from the generated code
options.rationale: Correct: recording captures routine steps and is a good way to see the object model, then refine the code.

options.text: For complex logic with loops and decisions across many files
options.rationale: Recorders cannot capture loops or conditional logic well.

options.text: Whenever you want error handling built in automatically
options.rationale: Recorders do not add error handling.

options.text: Never; recording produces no usable code
options.rationale: Recorded code is usable and often a helpful starting point.

items.explanation: Correct: recording captures routine steps and is a good way to see the object model, then refine the code.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make VBA more reliable and maintainable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Turn on Option Explicit and declare variables
options.rationale: Correct: it catches typos and undeclared variables at compile time.

options.text: Act on ranges directly instead of using .Select and ActiveCell
options.rationale: Correct: avoiding Select makes code faster and less fragile.

options.text: Enable all macros from any source by default
options.rationale: That is a security risk, not a reliability practice.

options.text: Put all logic in one giant unbroken procedure
options.rationale: Breaking work into procedures improves readability and reuse.

items.explanation: Correct: it catches typos and undeclared variables at compile time.

items.stem: A macro-enabled file must be shared across a team with macro-security in mind. What is the appropriate step?

options.text: Save as .xlsm and digitally sign the project so recipients can trust it
options.rationale: Correct: a signed .xlsm lets users enable macros based on a trusted publisher.

options.text: Save as .xlsx to keep the macros embedded
Tell everyone to disable macro security entirely
options.rationale: Disabling security exposes users to malicious code.

options.text: Email the code as plain text to paste manually
options.rationale: That is error-prone and bypasses signing.

items.explanation: Correct: a signed .xlsm lets users enable macros based on a trusted publisher.
